paper.title: Design of a Neural Network to Predict Team Performance in Acute Ischemic Stroke
paper.doi: not reported (no DOI in the PDF; author-hosted PDF at http://mcareapps.com/docs/design_neural_network_stroke_pathway.pdf)
paper.venue: not reported in the PDF (no journal name, volume or DOI on any page)
paper.capsule: Code Ocean capsule 3269870 'Neural Network for Predicting Stroke Team Performance'

claims.text: A three-layered TensorFlow network using four features (duration, NIHSS severity, age, hour of day) predicts door-to-needle time > 45 min on a held-out validation set with precision 63%, recall 67%, F1 0.64 and accuracy 60%.
The four input features are only weakly associated with door-to-needle time individually, yet the network builds a 'reasonable' prediction model from them.
The network has a 4-6-1 architecture trained with learning rate 0.15 and L2 penalty lambda 0.02.
Learning rate 0.15, layer sizes 4/6/1 and lambda 0.02 were selected as the optimum, giving training-set accuracy 60%, precision 68%, recall 71%, F1 0.68.
The 45-minute cut-off was chosen because it 'showed the best predictive performance'.
A neural network for optimising acute stroke care from a predictive model 'has not so far been reported in literature'.
The trained network is deployable as a simple predictor (JavaScript implementation with stored weights) that returns 0/1 for a 4-value input.

findings.evidence: The paper reports 'F1 (validation)' = 0.64 % (Abstract, p.1); the authors' own stored output (results/predict-output.txt) gives 62. Our re-run gives 63.16, which matches neither.
findings.question_for_authors: Which run produced the reported value of 'F1 (validation)' (0.64), given that results/predict-output.txt gives 62?

findings.evidence: The paper reports 'training-set F1' = 0.68 % (Hyperparameter tuning, p.4); the authors' own stored output (results/Output) gives 68. Our re-run gives 71.54, which matches neither.
findings.question_for_authors: Which run produced the reported value of 'training-set F1' (0.68), given that results/Output gives 68?

findings.evidence: With the paper's own choices the claim 'The network beats the majority-class baseline on the validation set (accuracy 60% vs 55.7%)' does not hold on re-run (effect = -1.6393442622950758).
findings.question_for_authors: Which settings or data version produced the reported result?

findings.evidence: The paper reports 'precision (validation)' = 63 % (Abstract, p.1); the authors' own stored output (results/predict-output.txt) gives 62. Our re-run gives 57.14, which matches neither. The gap is small (<5%): it may be run-to-run variation if the stored output came from a different run.
findings.question_for_authors: Which run produced the reported value of 'precision (validation)' (63), given that results/predict-output.txt gives 62?

findings.evidence: No dependency specification found (requirements.txt, environment.yml, renv.lock, ...).
findings.question_for_authors: Which software and library versions were used?

findings.evidence: [G2] Are inclusion/exclusion rules stated, with counts removed at each step? -> not_reported. No inclusion/exclusion rules and no counts removed at each step; the paper does not say whether all thrombolysis cases in the period were used.
findings.question_for_authors: Are inclusion/exclusion rules stated, with counts removed at each step?

findings.evidence: [G4] Is the outlier definition and removal rule stated (and applied before or after splitting)? -> not_reported. No outlier rule stated and none implemented in code.
findings.question_for_authors: Is the outlier definition and removal rule stated (and applied before or after splitting)?

findings.evidence: [M8] Were baselines given comparable tuning effort and the same data? -> not_reported. No baseline model (e.g. logistic regression, majority class, single feature) is reported; the 60% accuracy is not compared with anything.
findings.question_for_authors: Were baselines given comparable tuning effort and the same data?

findings.evidence: The first line of data/test_data.csv is already data (12,74,60,3,1), but code/nn.py:16 reads it with read_csv() and the default header setting, so that observation becomes the column names. The file has 61 data lines; the code sees 60. Every count, metric and split built on this table is one row short.
findings.question_for_authors: Is the first row of test_data.csv meant to be data? With the default header setting it is dropped.

findings.evidence: The first line of data/train_data.csv is already data (12,70,105,13,1), but code/nn.py:14 reads it with read_csv() and the default header setting, so that observation becomes the column names. The file has 221 data lines; the code sees 220. Every count, metric and split built on this table is one row short.
findings.question_for_authors: Is the first row of train_data.csv meant to be data? With the default header setting it is dropped.

findings.evidence: [G1] Is the exact data source identified (version, DOI, accession, download date)? -> partial. Single-centre historical records 2003-2018; no data dictionary, no per-row dates, no statement of how the 221/61 rows were extracted from the records.
findings.question_for_authors: Is the exact data source identified (version, DOI, accession, download date)?

findings.evidence: [G3] Is the handling of missing values stated? -> not_reported. No missing-value handling stated; the released csv files contain no missing cells, so the analysed subset may already be complete-case.
findings.question_for_authors: Is the handling of missing values stated?

findings.evidence: [G5] Is the sample size justified (power analysis or other rationale)? -> not_reported. No sample-size or power justification for 221 training / 61 validation cases.
findings.question_for_authors: Is the sample size justified (power analysis or other rationale)?

findings.evidence: [M1] Are random seeds stated, and are results reported over several seeds? -> partial. Only the Xavier initializer is seeded (seed=1); no seed for the TF graph, data order or the run; single run reported, no seed-to-seed variability.
findings.question_for_authors: Are random seeds stated, and are results reported over several seeds?

findings.evidence: [M3] How was the data split, and does the split respect groups (patients, compositions, scaffolds, time, sites)? -> partial. Temporal split (earlier years train, last 2 years validation) is stated, but the code additionally uses only the first 50% of test_data.csv as the in-training test set and the paper never mentions this second split.
findings.question_for_authors: How was the data split, and does the split respect groups (patients, compositions, scaffolds, time, sites)?

findings.evidence: [M5] Are hyperparameter search space, budget and selection criterion stated (selected on validation, not test)? -> partial. Learning rate, layer sizes and lambda are said to be chosen on training/validation performance, but no search grid, budget or selection criterion is reported, and the code contains no search loop.
findings.question_for_authors: Are hyperparameter search space, budget and selection criterion stated (selected on validation, not test)?
